question.:question/worked-solution:
A normal vector to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,0,0)$ can be found by computing 
$∇f(1,0,0).$ 

So, we first find the gradient and evaluate it at $(x,y,z)=(1,0,0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\text{ }j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{e}^{y}+y{e}^{z}+z{e}^{x})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{e}^{y}+y{e}^{z}+z{e}^{x})\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x{e}^{y}+y{e}^{z}+z{e}^{x})\,k \\  & =({e}^{y}+z{e}^{x})\,i+(x{e}^{y}+{e}^{z})\,j+(y{e}^{z}+{e}^{x})\,k \\ ∇f(1,0,0) & =({e}^{0}+(0){e}^{1})i+((1){e}^{0}+{e}^{0})j+((0){e}^{0}+{e}^{1})k \\  & =1\,i+2\,j+ek\end{aligned}
